samples.summary: Headline outcome ("Increase then Decrease leaves the cell exactly as it started") is knowingly not met for grouped values and user-chosen `nf: 'number'`
samples.evidence: The task doc's outcome is absolute: "Increase decimal places followed by Decrease decimal places must leave a cell exactly as it started — including leaving no dp/nf behind" (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-5). The implementation's `unsetKeepsRendering` gate means any value ≥ 1000 (`1234.5`) keeps a `{dp, nf:'number'}` residue after an equal number of increases/decreases — asserted as intended by the new test 'should keep the grouping separators the step would flatten' (packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:96-113) and recorded as a 'Known deviation' in the todo (:87-89) and in sheet-style.md:262-266. The deviation is documented and argued for, but it is a partial fulfilment of the stated outcome rather than the outcome; a reviewer/verifier should confirm the deviation was accepted on the issue (#845) and not just self-granted in the task file.

samples.summary: Spill-metadata preservation in `compactCell` (plus its new test file) is an unrelated bug fix bundled into the decimal round-trip change
samples.evidence: The diff adds spillRows/spillCols/spillAnchor/spillBlocked passthrough to `compactCell` and a whole new suite (packages/sheets/test/model/style-mutation.test.ts) about spill survival through style-only writes. Nothing in the originating task (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md 'The change' / 'Tasks') asks for this; it fixes a pre-existing data-loss path shared with `setStyle`/`clearCellStylesInRange` (sheet.ts:2007). It is defensible because `unsetRangeStyleValues` writes cells through `compactCell`, but it changes behavior for every existing style write and belongs in its own change/issue where the calculator's spill contract (docs/design/sheets/calculator.md:59-66) can be reviewed alongside it.

samples.summary: `selectionTargets()` duplicates an idiom already inlined twice in the same file instead of replacing it
samples.evidence: The new private `selectionTargets()` is exactly the expression already written inline at sheet.ts:3736-3738 (`setRangeStyle`) and :3757-3759 (`resetRangeStyleToDefault`), which the diff leaves untouched. Extracting the helper is the right direction; leaving the two older copies means three spellings of the same rule.

samples.summary: The cell-scan loop in `unsetRangeStyleValues` re-implements the existing getGrid/anchor/visited traversal used by `applyStylePatchToExistingCells` and `clearCellStylesInRange`
samples.evidence: sheet.ts:4380-4432 repeats verbatim the pattern at sheet.ts:1954-1968 and :1991-2013 (getGrid → parseRef → normalizeRefToAnchor → visited set → store.get → compactCell → delete-or-set). A shared private traversal helper would avoid a third copy of the anchor/dedup rules, which are easy to drift.

samples.summary: ~200 lines of layer-manipulation policy added inline to the 4500-line sheet.ts rather than to the existing style modules
samples.evidence: The repo already factors style-layer logic into `range-styles.ts` (mergeStylePatch, and now omitStyleKeys) and `style-mutation.ts` (pruning, compaction). `unsetRangeStyleValues`, `unsetKeepsRendering` and `selectionRendersAt` are pure-ish predicates over layers/grids that could live beside them, keeping sheet.ts as orchestration. Only the 12-line `omitStyleKeys` was extracted.

samples.summary: Removing `dp: 2` from `DefaultStyleValues` is a repo-wide persistence change made for one feature's benefit
samples.evidence: `dp: 2` is no longer pruned as a redundant default, so every path that writes `dp: 2` (e.g. xlsx style import, docs/design/sheets/xlsx-style-import.md:128-131; the visual harness fixtures at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/format-scenarios.tsx:330-342) now persists the key. The rationale is recorded in sheet-style.md:255-259 and in the change's own comment, and the reasoning is sound, but it widens the blast radius of a decimal-button fix into the shared style-pruning contract; worth calling out explicitly rather than only as an aside in the doc's 'Consequences'.

verdict.reason: Evidence verified in-tree. The task doc states an absolute outcome (todo.md:3-5: round trip must leave the cell exactly as it started, leaving no dp/nf behind), but changeDecimals gates the unset on unsetKeepsRendering (sheet.ts:4211-4229, 4275-4302), which returns false whenever dropping nf:'number' would change rendering — true for any grouped value (1234.5 -> '1,234.5'). The fall-through explicit write (sheet.ts:4231-4235) therefore leaves a {dp, nf:'number'} residue on a previously unstyled cell. This is asserted as intended by decimals.test.ts:94-112 and 114-127, and recorded only as a self-granted 'Known deviation' in todo.md:78-89 and sheet-style.md:262-265; sheet-style.md:216-218 still asserts the absolute claim, contradicting its own :262-265 bullet. No evidence in the repo that issue #845 accepted the deviation. Real, in-lane (spec conformance to the originating outcome), and major per the rubric: an unmet acceptance criterion.
